# Task 3 "Validate frame": funded round 1, CR re-review, and stop

**Current position:**
- The ordinary CR loop has ended. Review 3 was `DIVERGING`, so no convergence exception applies.
- The one escalated round has run, and its CR re-review was still `FIX_FIRST`.
- That puts this task into funded rounds under `reference/fix-loop.md`.
- I decode `**Amend-grant:** fund 2 fix rounds` using **Value decoding** in the amendment surface's Standing grants. I have not read that file here, so I take N = 2 funded rounds without reconstructing its text.
- Task 3's ledger starts at spent = 0.
- No `plan_tracker` write is made. Task 3 stays `in_progress`, and the phase stays `implement`.

## 1. Before the funded dispatch

Touched owner: task 3 only, since this is a singleton wave. I print:

```
funded round 1 of 2 for task 3
```

**Tree-before.** The Fix-delta tree-before is the tree recorded, keyed by this wave, when the escalated round's CR re-review was dispatched. It already exists, so nothing is recorded now.

## 2. Funded dispatch 1

This is a plain in-place repair worker in the branch checkout:
- It repeats the escalated payload and isolation exactly.
- It does not set `worktree: true` because the wave is integrated and uncommitted.
- It contains no commit or staging instruction.

```ts
subagent({
  agent: "implementer",
  model: "<configured-impl-model>",      // gauntlet_setting({ key: "escalationLoop" }).implModel
  context: "fresh",
  async: false,
  cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `<original task 3 "Validate frame" text, verbatim>
<Leg / Rules context as carried on every dispatch>
<task 3 Spec: anchors + absolute spec path>
<prior patch (integrated wave delta vs WAVE_BASE_SHA)>
SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: node --test frame.test.mjs
TEST_CONTRACT: <task 3 Tests: block verbatim + Files: Create:/Test: paths>
<status protocol: DONE | DONE_WITH_CONCERNS | BLOCKED | NEEDS_CONTEXT>

## Previous review report (re-review trigger)
<complete CR report from the escalated round's re-review, verbatim -
 FIX_FIRST; src/frame.ts:21 - missing length guard; Behaviour-change: no;
 TRAJECTORY: DIVERGING (3 -> 3, max severity Moderate)>`
})
```

The fix spends 1 of 2 funded rounds whatever the outcome. The supplied observation is that it returns `DONE`.

## 3. Scoped test gate, staging, and Fix-delta tree-after

```bash
(cd "/workspace/project" && node --test frame.test.mjs)
git -C /workspace/project add -A
```

Then I run the whole fix-delta block in one call. I stop dispatch if it exits nonzero.

```bash
FD_ROOT='/workspace/project'
FD_INDEX=$(mktemp) || exit 1
cp "$(git -C "$FD_ROOT" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path index)" "$FD_INDEX" || { rm -f "$FD_INDEX"; exit 1; }
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$FD_INDEX" git -C "$FD_ROOT" add -A && GIT_INDEX_FILE="$FD_INDEX" git -C "$FD_ROOT" write-tree
FD_STATUS=$?
rm -f "$FD_INDEX"
exit "$FD_STATUS"
```

I keep the printed SHA as this wave's tree-after and produce the delta:

```bash
git -C /workspace/project diff --binary <tree-before> <tree-after>
```

The delta is nonempty per the observation, so a re-review is dispatched.

## 4. CR re-review

The triggering report says `Behaviour-change: no`, so the re-review is CR only and does not reroute through SR.

```ts
subagent({
  agent: "code-reviewer",
  async: false,
  cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `<filled ../requesting-code-review/code-reviewer.md>
DESCRIPTION: funded fix round 1 for task 3 "Validate frame" (missing length guard)
PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS: <wave task 3 text from the plan>
BASE_SHA: <WAVE_BASE_SHA>
HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE
SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: node --test frame.test.mjs
<Leg / Rules context>

## Previous review report (re-review trigger)
<complete escalated-round CR report, verbatim>

<trajectory block from code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md "Re-review: trajectory verdict", verbatim>

## Fix delta
<output of git diff --binary <tree-before> <tree-after>>`
})
```

Supplied result: `FIX_FIRST`, `TRAJECTORY: STAGNANT (repeat of: missing length guard)`, with the same finding at `src/frame.ts:21`.

## 5. Next parent action: stop

The funded outcome table says any funded re-review reporting `STAGNANT` stops immediately, regardless of funding remaining. So round 2 is not dispatched, even though one funded round is left.

**What does not happen:**
- No `git commit` or `reset --soft`, because there is no wave commit.
- No `plan_tracker` update. Task 3 stays `in_progress`.
- No further tasks start.
- Phase stays `implement`.

**Stop note.** I apply `../brainstorming/reference/menu-layout.md`, which I have not read here, so I don't reconstruct it. I emit inline:

```
gauntlet: question
Stopped on task 3 (Validate frame); escalated round on <configured-impl-model> did not resolve it.

Problem: frame validation still reads the frame without checking its length first, so short or truncated input is not rejected; repeated fixes have not closed it.
budget: 1 of 2 spent
  src/frame.ts:21 - missing length guard

Fix options:
  a) add an explicit length check at src/frame.ts:21 that rejects a frame shorter than the required header/payload length before any field is read
  b) amend plan task 3 (or its spec anchor) to state exactly what minimum length and error behaviour a short frame must produce, then re-run the task against that contract

Pick one, or give another fix.
```

The turn ends here.

Below, `${…}` in dispatch text means literal expansion of the supplied verbatim material, not a summary. `CR_ESCALATED_TREE` is the tree recorded at the escalated CR’s dispatch; `WAVE_BASE_SHA` remains the original recorded wave base.

### 1. First funded repair


Dispatch one in-place repair worker, preserving the escalated repair’s payload and isolation. No worktree fan-out and no commit or staging instruction:

```javascript
SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS:
node --test frame.test.mjs

## Previous review report (re-review trigger)
${COMPLETE_ESCALATED_CR_REPORT_VERBATIM}`

```

The prior report is the escalated CR report, including its `FIX_FIRST`, `Behaviour-change: no`, `TRAJECTORY: DIVERGING (3 -> 3, max severity Moderate)`, and `src/frame.ts:21 - missing length guard` finding. Insert the complete supplied report, not only those lines.

### 2. Scoped gate and review-tree capture

After the supplied `DONE` result, run:

```bash

```

After that passes, stage the deliverables and capture the review tree:

```bash
git -C "/workspace/project" add -A
```

```bash
FD_ROOT='/workspace/project'
FD_INDEX=$(mktemp) || exit 1
cp "$(git -C "$FD_ROOT" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path index)" "$FD_INDEX" || { rm -f "$FD_INDEX"; exit 1; }
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$FD_INDEX" git -C "$FD_ROOT" add -A && GIT_INDEX_FILE="$FD_INDEX" git -C "$FD_ROOT" write-tree

rm -f "$FD_INDEX"
exit "$FD_STATUS"
```

Record the printed SHA as `CR_FUNDED_1_TREE`, keyed to this wave. Stop on any shell error. Produce the fix delta from the prior review’s recorded tree, not from a commit range:

```bash
git -C "/workspace/project" diff --binary \
  "$CR_ESCALATED_TREE" "$CR_FUNDED_1_TREE"
```

Use that command’s complete output as `${FUNDED_1_FIX_DELTA}` below. The scenario supplies a nonempty tracked delta.

### 3. Funded-round CR re-review

`Behaviour-change: no` means CR only; do not insert an SR dispatch. Review the current integrated checkout against the unchanged wave base:

```javascript
subagent({
  agent: "code-reviewer",
  context: "fresh",
  async: false,
  cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `Use the requesting-code-review/code-reviewer.md template.

${TASK_3_IMPLEMENTATION_AND_REPAIR_DESCRIPTION}

PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS:
${ORIGINAL_TASK_3_TEXT_AND_SPEC_ANCHORS_VERBATIM}

BASE_SHA: ${WAVE_BASE_SHA}
HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE

SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS:
node --test frame.test.mjs

Review the integrated staged and unstaged wave diff in /workspace/project.
Do not modify source files.

## Previous review report (re-review trigger)
${COMPLETE_ESCALATED_CR_REPORT_VERBATIM}

## Fix delta
${FUNDED_1_FIX_DELTA}

If your task contains a "Previous review report (re-review trigger)" section
and you found issues, append exactly one more line after Behaviour-change: —
this line, not Behaviour-change:, is the true final line of the report:

TRAJECTORY: CONVERGING (<n_prev> -> <n_now>, max severity <X>)
TRAJECTORY: DIVERGING
TRAJECTORY: STAGNANT (repeat of: <finding>)

Pick the first label that applies, in this order:

1. STAGNANT: a previous Critical or Moderate finding survives materially unchanged — name it.
2. DIVERGING: <n_now> >= <n_prev>, or the fix introduced a new Critical or Moderate finding.
3. CONVERGING: otherwise — the Critical/Moderate count fell, no new Critical or
   Moderate appeared, and every surviving Critical or Moderate was materially improved.

<n_prev>/<n_now> count Critical and Moderate findings only; Minors — ride-along
Minors declined or unchanged, and (outside fix delta) downgrades alike — never
move the TRAJECTORY: line. <X> is the highest remaining severity. For this line
the severity set is exactly Critical/Moderate/Minor, regardless of vocabulary
used elsewhere in your report.

The orchestrator dispatches one extra fix only when this line says CONVERGING
without "max severity Critical" — be accurate, not generous.

If you found no issues, report success as usual and omit this line.
First reviews (no previous-report section) omit this line.`
})
```
